skirmishes.place: Same time window: River (we took it)
Same time window: Mini Prime (we took it)
Same time window: Fangtooth (we took it)

notes: The kills in this window fell on opposite sides of the map (offlane and mid lane): two separate plays, not one fight.
Enemy had 1 healer; only 1 of us carried anti-heal — usually wants two vs a heal comp.
Their main damage was Mourn (7k magical); 0/5 of us itemized magic resist — that hurt.
Enemy ran 0/5 on or near their meta core — they were off-meta too, the win was there.

draftNote: 2 of five queued off a bottom-two lane: Goldilocks324 (support→midlane), Cuban Noobster (offlane→carry).

coaching.headline: Thirteen kills, zero deaths, every Fangtooth. That was a clean fucking clinic.
coaching.team: We took all but one river buff, both Fangtooths, the Mini Prime and all three seedlings, and our side took zero deaths. All four recorded fights went our way, and the two game-defining fights landed in the same windows as our Mini Prime and second Fangtooth. That was a squad stomp from start to finish.

focus.title: Fight on the timer, take the prize
focus.action: When a Fangtooth or Prime timer is close, group up and take the fight in that window, like the two here. Once the fight is won, the objective comes before the next chase.

10.8.call: Four kills to none with Belica, Rampage and Steel credited, and the Mini Prime was ours shortly after. Win the exchange near the timer, then take the prize. This is the version to repeat.

13.5.call: Belica and Steel took kills on Crunch and Sparrow, and the second Fangtooth was ours shortly after, with zero deaths on our side.

matchup: Skylar and Steel faced Sparrow and Mourn; the enemy duo took two early deaths and Skylar never died.
Countess's Feast suppress and Crunch's Forward Crunch dash stun were the threats to Skylar's position.
build: Sky Splitter pays most against healthy targets in longer exchanges, and Hypercharge shots also apply it.
It was the only completed item, so this match tests very little; the winning core runs Plasma Blade, Vanquisher and Imperator.
eternal: Thraex, Savage Strikes and Ferocity reward staying on one target from a safe firing spot.
Golden Mane is the defensive draft alternative to Ferocity, trading ramping attack speed for less damage from single-target hits.
augment: Assault MK-II deepens the airborne plan: longer hover and an additional missile with each attack.
Suppressive Fire is the alternative for more basic-attack range while hovering, giving up the extra missile.
crest: Ortus pays when activated right before a fight; two assists gave the permanent bonus at most two takedowns to feed it.
improvement: No build change is proven: one completed item and zero deaths.
Sky Splitter's current-health damage fits a durable front line of Crunch, Countess and Mourn.
If targets are mostly squishy, the Plasma Blade crit core trades current-health damage for crits and the Vanquisher execute.

matchup: Steel has answers to both Sparrow and Mourn: Force Shield destroys projectiles, and Bull Rush, Shield Bash and Shield Slam stun.
The enemy duo had two deaths early and ours had none.
build: Fire Blossom suits a support who stands inside the fight and feeds Hybrid Defence's magical armor.
It was the only completed item, so the rest of the core is untested in this match.
eternal: Cannibalism adds permanent maximum health on takedowns, which Steel's kills and assists fed.
Voracity pays on unit kills, but farming minions is not Steel's job.
Regenerative Tissue is the alternative to Voracity, suiting a support who resets between fights.
augment: Heavy Metal scales with Steel's total armor, so Fire Blossom and the Hybrid Defence conversion both add to it.
Adaptive Force is the alternative, trading damage for more projectile blocking against Sparrow.
crest: Rift Walkers' pull is a natural setup for Steel's stuns, plus extra ward capacity.
The ward capacity is the part of the crest fully under Steel's control.
improvement: Keep the tank core: Hybrid Defence converts Fire Blossom's physical armor into magical armor, and Steel never died.
Tainted Charm would add a second anti-heal source against Mourn, though it carries no armor for Heavy Metal.

matchup: Scarlett took first blood on Crunch and killed Crunch again late without dying.
Crunch is a melee diver with a dash stun, a knockup and stun, and Re-Crunch healing.
Countess's Feast suppress and Mourn's pull and healing were the other threats.
build: Tainted Blade cuts Mourn's healing and Crunch's Re-Crunch sustain, and was the team's only anti-heal item.
Mutilator adds maximum-health damage, applied several times through ability hits on heroes, plus omnivamp.
eternal: Marrow and Blood Bank add healing and lifesteal from hero damage, and Roses grows takedown gold and boosts Marrow after hero kills.
Roses suits a game where Scarlett kept collecting takedowns without dying.
The Maw is the alternative to Roses, adding true damage against low-health targets instead of takedown gold.
augment: Volcaic Slam's slow depends on first landing Ashen Vow's outer edge to get Empowered Cindara.
Scarlet Dawn is the alternative, trading the slow for more First Intent dashes and shields.
crest: Pacifier's empowered hit applies to Scarlett's physical damage, and the reset after a hero kill suits a finisher.
improvement: Scarlett had no magical armor against three magical enemies but never died, so the match shows no cost.
If Neon, Countess or Mourn start winning the brawls, a later magical armor item trades damage for survival.
Keep Tainted Blade while Mourn is healing; it was the team's only anti-heal.

matchup: Countess died once; Rampage's kills landed on Crunch, Neon and Mourn twice.
Mourn's Tainted Charm reduces healing on nearby enemies, a direct problem for a sustain jungler.
build: Overlord and Basilisk both reward staying on targets with basic attacks.
The recorded winning core is Overlord, Rapture and Cursed Scroll; Basilisk takes a core slot with armor shred and ability haste.
eternal: Krix, Regenerative Tissue and Feeding Frenzy, with Tiny Titan, lean hard into basic-attack brawling among enemies.
Cannibalism is the alternative to Feeding Frenzy, trading attack speed for permanent health from takedowns.
augment: Tiny Titan trades taking more damage for attack speed, suiting Overlord's cleave and Basilisk's shred.
Rampage took the most damage on our team and never died, so the trade held.
Rock & Awe is the alternative, adding Boulder Throw damage and keeping the normal Behemoth.
crest: Nyr Warboots' decaying movement speed and health regeneration work as both an engage and an exit for a brawler.
improvement: Keep the core; Rampage never died, though Nyr Warboots supplies only a little magical armor against three magical enemies.
If Countess's or Neon's damage starts ending Behemoth early, compare Cursed Scroll, trading Basilisk's armor shred and ability haste.

matchup: Neon died once and finished with only Combustion.
Countess and Crunch were the dive threats able to reach Belica.
build: Noxia pays when a separate ability hits the mark, exactly the Seismic Assault into Void Bomb or Neural Disruptor pattern.
The build matches the recorded winning core minus Wraith Leggings.
eternal: Bottomless Vial pays on river buff kills; we took all but one, though the feed does not say who took each.
Philosopher is the alternative to Bottomless Vial for passive gold when river buffs are contested.
augment: Combat Veteran is a levels-first choice, and Belica's farm already ran above the norm.
Pulsefire Rounds is the alternative, adding on-hit damage to basic attacks but giving up the passive experience.
crest: Soulbearer is Belica's defensive tool if Countess or Crunch reach the backline; Belica never died.
improvement: On core; nothing in this match tests the build.
Wraith Leggings is the natural next item; the lower hero damage rate does not point at an item swap.

a2319134-808e-4456-853f-cf3a14be22fc: Zero deaths on the carry. Skylar farmed above the recorded norm and cleared two enemy wards, the most on our team. Staying alive all game is the baseline, and Skylar hit it.
Hero damage ran well under the recorded Skylar norm, a quiet fucking afternoon for the carry in a stomp. Next fight, use the longer Assault MK-II hover to shoot heroes from behind Steel and Scarlett.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 ran the support job properly: Steel never died, Skylar never died, and the early double on Sparrow and Mourn left the enemy duo two deaths down before the ten-minute mark. Most wards on our team too.
Rift Walkers gives Steel a third ward slot. Next game, put that spare ward on the approach to each Fangtooth and Prime before the team walks in.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster took first blood on Crunch, killed Crunch again late and never died, with our second-highest hero damage. Crunch finished on five deaths and no completed item, and Scarlett started that misery.
Tainted Blade was our only anti-heal. When Mourn starts healing a brawl, put physical hits on the healed target if Scarlett can reach that target without leaving Skylar and Belica uncovered.
e6883bce-af43-4199-9d79-d7125804b8e3: Rampage ate the most damage on our team, more than doubled anyone else's objective damage and never died. Four kills, Mourn twice. That is a jungler walking into the shit and strolling back out.
When Mourn is close, Tainted Charm cuts Rampage's healing, and Tiny Titan already makes Behemoth take extra damage. Go in with Steel's or Belica's stun ready rather than trusting the regen alone.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Farm that turns up at objectives is the whole fucking job. Willy Guggenheim farmed Belica well above the recorded norm, never died, and had kill credit in both the Mini Prime and Fangtooth windows.
Hero damage rate still sat under the recorded Belica norm. With that much farm, lead with the Seismic Assault stun so Void Bomb and Neural Disruptor land on a target that cannot walk away.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s), Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s), Mourn Abduct (pull). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 1 item of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Countess, Crunch. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Plasma Grenade → Hypercharge on-hit → Air Assault reposition → Atomiser ult
ourKits.winCondition: Hypercharge and kite-shoot from Air Assault safety
ourKits.passive: extra jump; kills cause corpse explosions
ourKits.playWith: a frontline so she can free-fire airborne
ourKits.playAgainst: CC her out of Air Assault; she's squishy on the ground

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

ourKits.combo: Pounce → Rumble slow → Boulder Throw → Behemoth ult to brawl
ourKits.winCondition: engage with Pounce, grow with Behemoth and out-sustain the fight
ourKits.passive: ramping health regen for jungle sustain
ourKits.playWith: follow-up damage while he front-lines and CCs
ourKits.playAgainst: anti-heal and kiting beat his sustain brawl; burst him before Behemoth

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

enemyKits.combo: Shadow Slip in → Eventide → Blade Siphon → Feast suppress ult, Haemorrhage true-damage
enemyKits.winCondition: Feast-suppress a squishy and delete them with true-damage burst
enemyKits.passive: two-ability hits apply a %max-HP true-damage bleed
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up after her pick
enemyKits.playAgainst: Feast is her whole engage — bait it / peel; she's fragile, punish the recast window

enemyKits.combo: Forward Crunch gap-close stun → Right Crunch knockup → empowered Left Crunch, sustain via Re-Crunch
enemyKits.winCondition: all-in a squishy with the empowered combo and heal back through Re-Crunch
enemyKits.passive: post-ability empowered basic that refunds cooldowns
enemyKits.playWith: peel-stripping engage so he reaches the backline
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel/CC him off — without resets he's stranded; anti-heal blunts Re-Crunch

enemyKits.combo: Abduct pull → Contagion ally-heal bugs → Beguile damage-reduction → Eclipse vision-denial ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and sustain the team through the brawl
enemyKits.playWith: burst that punishes his pulled target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect the long Abduct channel/range; anti-heal blunts Contagion

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first
